study type: Retrospective study combined with economic model development and literature review
exposure: Misoprostol vaginal insert (MVI) for induction of labor (IOL)
Alternative technologies for IOL (standard of care)
outcome: Length of patients' stay in hospital wards
cohort: The study included women with an unfavorable cervix, from 36 weeks of gestation, for whom induction of labor was clinically indicated.
finding: The use of misoprostol vaginal insert (MVI) for induction of labor was associated with reduced hospital staff time and shorter patient hospital stays, resulting in lower total costs compared to alternative technologies in most scenarios.
